nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong light over shallow, clear water lets seagrass and algae grow across the broad flats.

nodes.name: Cap Blanc upwelling
nodes.desc: Permanent upwelling at Cap Blanc brings nutrients that help make these waters among the richest fishing grounds in the region.

nodes.name: Windblown sediment
nodes.desc: Sediment blown in from the continent adds nutrients and organic matter to the shallow sea.

nodes.name: Tidal mudflats
nodes.desc: Vast intertidal flats and sand banks hold the seagrass beds and feed the wintering shorebirds.

nodes.name: Bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead seagrass, algae and animals, releasing nutrients back to the mud and water.

nodes.name: Dwarf eelgrass
nodes.desc: Seagrass of sheltered intertidal flats; its beds shelter invertebrates and young fish, and its dead leaves enrich the sediment.

nodes.name: Slender seagrass
nodes.desc: Seagrass of shallow sandy bottoms in the eastern Atlantic, forming meadows alongside dwarf eelgrass.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting and mud-surface microalgae fuelled by upwelled nutrients; they feed fish, clams and crabs.

nodes.name: Green sea turtle
nodes.desc: Adults graze mostly on seagrass and algae in shallow lagoons and bays. The species occurs at the site and is listed by the IUCN.

nodes.name: Lucine clam
nodes.desc: Small clam of seagrass sediments that lives with sulfide-eating bacteria; a principal prey of wintering red knots.

nodes.name: West African fiddler crab
nodes.desc: Burrowing crab of muddy flats that feeds on organic matter in the sediment and is itself prey for birds and octopus.

nodes.name: Flathead grey mullet
nodes.desc: Schooling fish of shallow coastal waters feeding on algae and detritus. Mullet are the main prey of Atlantic humpback dolphins.

nodes.name: Round sardinella
nodes.desc: Small schooling fish that eats plankton and is a major food for larger fish, seabirds and marine mammals in upwelling waters.

nodes.name: Common octopus
nodes.desc: Seabed hunter of crabs and shellfish; octopus and squid are the chief food of Mediterranean monk seals.

nodes.name: Red knot
nodes.desc: Long-distance migrant that winters on West African flats and in winter eats mainly hard-shelled prey such as bivalves.

nodes.name: Eurasian spoonbill
nodes.desc: Wading bird that sweeps its bill through shallows for small fish and crustaceans; the site is a major wintering ground.

nodes.name: Great white pelican
nodes.desc: Large fish-eating bird that breeds on the site's islands and fishes in the shallows.

nodes.name: Lesser black-backed gull
nodes.desc: Abundant gull of the flats and shores; it takes crabs and other shore prey and also preys on other waterbirds.

nodes.name: Western marsh harrier
nodes.desc: Raptor that hunts over the flats in winter and has been recorded taking shorebirds such as red knot.

nodes.name: Atlantic humpback dolphin
nodes.desc: Rare coastal dolphin that herds mullet and other inshore fish, sometimes towards Imraguen fishers' nets.

nodes.name: Mediterranean monk seal
nodes.desc: Rare seal of Cap Blanc, home to the largest surviving colony; it eats octopus, squid, mullet and sardines.

nodes.name: Blacktip shark
nodes.desc: Coastal shark that hunts schooling fish such as mullet and sardines. Sharks and rays in the park are under heavy fishing pressure.
